solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conversationalist passes to and fro, skipping tour (10)

indicators.note: the word goes one way and then back the other, so COL is followed by its own reversal
the letters of TOUR skip about into a new order

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
COL again, this time running back the other way

explanation.surface: A chatty traveller passes to and fro, giving the full tour a miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes' does double duty: one COL going forward and the same COL coming back, which is what 'to and fro' asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A collocutor is someone who takes part in a conversation, a conversationalist.

clue.text: Pisa bar is between two rivers — one tips there (9)

indicators.note: bar means except, so PISA without IS
PA sits between the two rivers

blocks.note: the Cam, the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A bar in Pisa sits between two rivers, where one drinker topples over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a place to drink in Pisa, but it means 'except'. The definition is cryptic: the Leaning Tower of Pisa is a bell tower, and it is the one that tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a bell tower, and the most famous one, at Pisa, leans.

clue.text: In due course answer line on the side (7)

explanation.surface: A promise to reply eventually, with a note in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one instruction, but it splits cleanly into three short pieces laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things at the side, like a sideways pass in football, are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Cleaner company fully reduced wood burned for fuel (8)

indicators.note: ALL, meaning fully, is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: a char is a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaning firm is scaled back entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is an old British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood heated with little air turns into a black fuel that burns hotter than the original timber.

clue.text: Road movie all the same — duo in convertible (6,3,6)

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed, so the letters are converted

explanation.surface: A road movie that is all the same: two people driving a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the film itself: its heroines are a duo who flee in a convertible. 'Convertible' is the car and also the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 1991 Ridley Scott film follows two women fleeing across America by car.

clue.text: Cheers after snitch finally given cane (6)

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so the thanks follow the informer in the answer
'finally' means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An informer is thanked and then beaten with a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is the British informal thank-you, TA, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the cane from a climbing palm, used for furniture.

clue.text: Remain tender and close to wife (4)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Stay loving and near to your wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' reads as an adjective of affection, but it is the noun: an offer or bid.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word surviving in 'bide your time': to stay put and wait.

clue.text: American sticks gift boxes in court (9)

blocks.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
the dock is the box where the accused stands in court

explanation.surface: An American hits a present, then throws punches in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' and 'boxes' both look like verbs; sticks is the countryside and boxes are the enclosures of a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The boondocks is American slang for remote backwoods country, the sticks.

clue.text: Taxonomist’s flies come down, time after time (7)

indicators.note: 'after' means following, so the second time follows the first in the answer

blocks.note: to dip is to come down
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Insects keep landing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' is two separate times, one abbreviated and one an ERA; the 'Taxonomist's' tag says a scientific name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the order of two-winged insects, the true flies, in biological classification.

clue.text: Drive four took after appropriate safety check (8)

indicators.note: IV and ATE come after MOT

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual safety test for a British car, the check appropriate to driving

explanation.surface: A driver takes the car out after the proper roadworthiness test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the compulsory yearly roadworthiness test for vehicles in the UK. 'Drive' looks like motoring, which fits the surface, but it means to spur on.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone is to push them into action by giving them a reason to act.

clue.text: Men have fun holding nothing back (6)

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside you, so SPORT takes O in
the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: to sport is to play or have fun

explanation.surface: Men enjoying themselves while holding nothing in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: SPO(O)RT read backwards gives the answer. 'Men' is the soldiers' sense: ordinary ranks as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are 'men' in military usage, as in 'officers and men'.

clue.text: Some land used for religious purposes out of bounds (4)

indicators.note: the bounds are the outer letters, which go

blocks.clueFragment: used for religious purposes out of bounds
blocks.note: SACRED loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Some church land is off limits to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' reads as forbidden, which suits sacred ground, but it tells you to strip the word's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of area, so any piece of ground measured out in it is some land.

clue.text: Grazing animals on accessible land sounded appropriate (10)

indicators.note: the wordplay is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: deer on a common, open land anyone may use

explanation.surface: Deer feeding on open public land made a noise that suited them.
explanation.walkthrough: A common is open land where the public may walk. 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to take something for one's own use, to appropriate it.

clue.text: Where Muslims legislate, does Buddhist sin? (9)

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
to sin is to be bad

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Buddhist would do wrong in an Islamic state.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'does Buddhist sin?' is paraphrased as 'IS LAMA BAD?', and the answer is read straight off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, an Islamic republic, where its parliament sits.

clue.text: Seeker of eternal life St Michael converted (9)

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: A saint was converted by someone hoping to live for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suits a saint, but here it rearranges his name; alchemists sought the elixir of life as well as gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists sought the elixir of life, which was to give immortality.

clue.text: Leave sons to prepare for exams (5)

blocks.note: to cram is to study hard just before an exam

explanation.surface: A parent leaves the boys alone to revise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a parent letting the boys be, but it is the command to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang imperative meaning go away at once, so the same as telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Old Americans get fatter — why not? (3,2,4)

blocks.note: the Maya, a pre-Columbian people of Central America
to swell is to grow bigger

explanation.surface: An ancient people put on weight, and who could blame them?
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls in a different place from the pieces: MAYA + SWELL is read as MAY AS WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: 'May as well' and 'why not?' both shrug agreement with a suggestion.

clue.text: Seed leaving red stain spoiled blue tent (5,3)

indicators.note: the letters are spoiled, knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A seed has left a red mark that ruined a blue tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The colours in the surface are a trap: blue is fodder, and the red stain belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The betel nut, the seed of the areca palm, is chewed and stains the mouth and spit red.

clue.text: Charlie in optimism brought round big date (5)

indicators.note: Charlie is placed in the other word, so C sits inside
HOPE is turned round, reading backwards

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, full of hope, came round for a big date.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPE reversed is EPOH, and C goes in before the H. 'Big date' is a date that marks the start of a new era, not a romantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a date marking the beginning of a notable period.

clue.text: Enter theatre from below a leafy canopy (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from below reverses the letters

explanation.surface: Actors come on stage from under a canopy of leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter theatre' is a stage direction in the surface; the two words are LOG and REP, and in a down clue 'from below' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a garden framework over which climbing plants grow to form a leafy canopy.

clue.text: Notice change coming across old queen’s foe (9)

indicators.note: VARY stretches across ERS, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A notice announces a change in the enemies of a former queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Regina is abbreviated ER, and the possessive 's supplies a real letter S. 'Notice' looks like a verb but is the noun, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an opponent or enemy in a contest or conflict.

clue.text: Now little-used part of foot has itch regularly (7)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Part of a foot is itching at regular intervals, and is rarely used now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now little-used' is a dictionary label for old words, which is exactly what archaic means.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic words are old-fashioned and rarely used today.

clue.text: Mad, not opening outlet in the run up to Christmas (6)

indicators.note: MAD without its opening letter

explanation.surface: Frantic shoppers, with a store shut, in the busy weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not opening' reads as a shop closed for business, which fits the Christmas rush; it means lose the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season of the four weeks before Christmas.

clue.text: Unromantic place upsetting for denizen (6,4)

indicators.note: the letters are upset, knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreary spot that a local resident finds upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fairly literal but modern: the friend zone is a place, figuratively, where romance is off the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The friend zone is the state of being seen only as a friend by someone you fancy.

clue.text: Mould turned inside out functions (4)

indicators.note: the inside letters move outside and the outside letters move in

explanation.surface: A casting mould is flipped over so its interior shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside out' is taken literally: the word's middle pair of letters becomes its outer shell, and its first and last letters go to the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to operate or work, as a device functions or acts.

clue.text: Trainee never gripping tool (6)

blocks.note: a vice is a clamping tool on a workbench

explanation.surface: An apprentice who never picks up a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' looks like a container instruction around 'tool', but it describes the tool: a vice grips.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a beginner still learning, like a monk or nun in training.

clue.text: Design the new hotel with the shape of an egg (8)

blocks.note: an inn is a small hotel

blocks.clueFragment: with the shape of an egg

explanation.surface: An architect plans a new hotel shaped like an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The new' reads as describing the hotel, but it belongs to the definition: to design the new is to innovate.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce or devise something new.

clue.text: Go on for the finale (4)

blocks.note: a noun: the final item, the end

explanation.surface: Carry on through to the grand finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings side by side, one a verb and one a noun, with 'for' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue; the last is the final part.

clue.text: Stage warm and later cold during test (10)

indicators.note: HEAT and C go inside TRIAL
C comes after HEAT, further along inside the test

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A test in which something is warmed and then chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' is an adjective here, as in stage effects. 'Later' tells you the cold arrives further along inside the test than the warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective sense: anything belonging to the theatre, as in stage lighting or stage makeup.
